On 18 November 2022, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology released the draft of the Personal Data Protection Bill, 2022. This bill provides for the processing of digital personal data in a manner that recognizes both the right of individuals to protect their personal data and the need to process personal data for lawful purposes. It is the first Act of the Parliament of India where "she/her" pronouns were used unlike the usual "he/him" pronouns.

The Personal Data Protection Bill, 2022 replaces the Information Technology (Reasonable security practices and procedures and sensitive personal data or information) Rules, 2011 and the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021. It focuses on the protection of personal data as a fundamental right and provides for the establishment of a Data Protection Authority for the protection of personal data.

In the context of copyright law, the Thai Copyright Act (NO.3) B.E. 2558 (2015) and Copyright Act (NO.4) B.E. 2561 (2018) define the rights of authors and the limitations on those rights. These acts cover reproduction, adaptation in part of a work or abridgement or making a summary, distribution, rental, lending, public performance, communication to the public, and making available of the work to the public.

In a study on the efficiency of pressure–volume work, it was revealed that although NLP (natural-language processing) models are capable of incredible feats, their abilities are very much limited by the amount of context they receive. This limitation could cause difficulties for researchers who hope to use them to do things such as analyze ancient languages. In some cases, there are not enough examples of a particular language or dialect available to train a model to accurately process and understand it.
